headline: Highest risk is medium: Continue can write shared workspace files and use MCP, while LightZero is read-only and non-networked, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can use MCP and write/read workspace files, so attacker-controlled content in shared files could influence its tool use. LightZero has no file or MCP surfaces, so it is not an active injector, but it can still be the source of content if its outputs are copied into the workspace. The shared-filesystem pathway makes this plausible in default IDE use.
conditions: IF Continue reads instructions from workspace files without provenance checks
IF LightZero-generated text is copied into a shared workspace file
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the session
Keep LightZero outputs out of shared workspace files
Use a separate directory per agent
Add a manual review step before any tool call
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can egress broadly, but LightZero has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no data classes touched. The pair therefore has a limited leakage path mainly through manual copying or shared files, not an automatic exfiltration channel from LightZero. The blast radius is small and mostly local to code in the workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive code is placed in a shared workspace file
IF Continue is configured to send workspace contents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the shared workspace
Use a local model provider for Continue
Restrict Continue to a narrow project folder
Rotate any exposed API keys after the session
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while LightZero is non-runnable and has no write or process capabilities. That means there is little direct write-write conflict; the main overlap is read/write on the same workspace via Continue only. Because LightZero cannot mutate shared state, the conflict pathway is weak and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator gives LightZero write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Do not grant LightZero write permissions
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use file backups before agent edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on tool outputs, but LightZero has no documented action-taking authority and no I/O surfaces, so there is no strong default chain where LightZero's output is automatically trusted and executed. Any cascade would require manual transfer of text from LightZero into Continue. That makes the pathway possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to local coding work.
conditions: IF a human copies LightZero output into Continue as authoritative instructions
IF Continue is allowed to execute tool calls based on unreviewed pasted text
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Do not paste model output directly into prompts
Use a checklist for code changes
Keep LightZero outputs separate from task instructions
requires-engineering: add verification gates for imported text

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. Continue is open-source and touches code/editor buffers; LightZero is open-source and has no data classes or residency claims. There is no documented PHI, EU PII, retention, or certification conflict to assess, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes not shown here
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair
Document data-class handling before deployment
Review retention settings if added later
